$comment: Subjects for the Avengers object-synthesis benchmark.
These ten packages are the pure-Python Pynguin corpus from Lukasczyk et al.,
'An empirical study of automated unit test generation for Python' (EMSE 2023).
They are NOT the DS-C corpus of Berg et al. (arXiv:2603.06107), which targets
C-extension modules; that paper is followed here for its crash handling and its
statistical protocol, not for its subjects. Saying which corpus a number came
from is the difference between a comparable result and a misleading one.
Two profiles. 'emse-3.10' pins the versions that study used, on the interpreter
it used, so coverage numbers are comparable to the published baseline.
'current-3.12' takes whatever installs today and exists for fast iteration and
smoke runs; its numbers are NOT comparable to the published ones.

The smoke set is codetiming (the case study) and docstring_parser. python-string-utils is deliberately not in it: every class it defines is private, so it has no object-synthesis subjects at all -- a fine thing for the full corpus to report, and a useless smoke test.
